title: Thai Yellow Coconut Curry with Prawns, Potatoes and Crispy Shallots
summary: Potatoes are parboiled, yellow curry paste is fried in thick coconut milk until the oil separates, then thinned coconut milk, palm sugar, fish sauce, potatoes, cherry tomatoes and prawns are simmered briefly and topped with crispy shallots.

ingredients.item: waxy potatoes, cut into 4 cm chunks

ingredients.note: check the label: most Thai curry pastes contain shrimp paste (crustaceans); choose a shrimp-free paste if you avoid it

ingredients.item: palm sugar or light brown sugar
large raw prawns, peeled and deveined

steps.title: Fry the shallots
steps.text: Heat 100 ml oil in a small pan over medium heat and fry the 3 sliced shallots, stirring, until light golden, 6 to 8 min. Lift onto kitchen paper to crisp; keep 1 tbsp of the oil.

steps.title: Parboil the potatoes
steps.text: Simmer 450 g potato chunks in unsalted water until just tender, 10 to 12 min, and drain.

steps.title: Fry the paste
steps.text: Heat the 1 tbsp shallot oil in a wide pan, add 60 g yellow curry paste and the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk in two or three additions, and fry, stirring, until it darkens and the oil separates, about 5 min.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Stir in 10 g palm sugar, 2 tsp fish sauce, the rest of the coconut milk and 120 ml water. Add the potatoes and 100 g cherry tomatoes and simmer 5 min.

steps.title: Cook the prawns
steps.text: Add 600 g prawns and simmer until pink, opaque and 63 °C, 3 to 4 min.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Top with the crispy shallots and serve with jasmine rice.

tips: Lift the shallots out when light gold; they darken off the heat.
Do not overcook the prawns or they turn tough.
Taste before adding more fish sauce; pastes vary.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour and eat within 1 day, reheated gently until piping hot. Keep the shallots separate and airtight. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
